_meta.notes: v1 was 6 LIVE government URLs. Four were hub or JS-rendered pages the extractor cannot read, so the set measured almost nothing, and a network failure made the run pass vacuously. v2 is backed by HTML snapshots under ./pages/, captured byte-for-byte as fetch_url_content sees them (raw and unstripped - the <head>/nav bloat IS the thing under test). Every anchor in 'must_contain_in_parsed' was machine-verified against its committed snapshot on 2026-08-12; none is asserted from memory. 'min_parsed_chars' sits at roughly 60-70% of observed parsed length, so a parser regression fails while an ordinary page edit does not. 'discriminates_vs_raw' records whether the anchors are ABSENT from the first 24000 chars of raw HTML - i.e. whether this fixture can tell the pre-fix extractor apart from the fixed one; it was measured, not assumed. requirement_type is deliberately blank in expected_facts because LLM type assignment is not stable run to run, so this set measures CONTENT recall rather than classification. The deterministic gate is backend/tests/test_requirement_extraction_parse_gate.py; this file also drives the report-only LLM eval.

curation_note: expected_facts were corrected on 2026-08-12 after a baseline run scored 0.00/0.00 here. The original expectation was 'national identity number' — the page's TOPIC, not anything it requires of you. The page states its actual obligations as reporting a move to Norway and undergoing an ID check; both phrases are present in the parsed text. Fixing an expectation that never described a requirement is curation, not tuning to pass.

discrimination_note: Cannot discriminate, and that is the correct record rather than a gap. The whole page is 28KB, so its body already sat inside the extractor's 24000-char raw window - which is why cleiss.fr was the ONE source that still produced facts in the 2026-08-12 pre-fix run (6 facts, while every skatteetaten/udi/nav/politiet URL produced 0). Kept as a positive fixture because it is the only non-Norwegian authority and the only French-language page in the set.

notes: NEGATIVE FIXTURE. politiet.no is a genuine JS-only shell: <main> is an empty container and the content streams in escaped Next.js RSC payloads, so the parser yields 0 characters. Pins that the pipeline produces NOTHING here rather than hallucinating facts out of nav chrome - which is exactly the failure that let the v1 FR-NO entry pass at 1.0/1.0 while never reading a page body.
